evidence.statement: All order routes require an authenticated caller (group RequireAuthorization()). GET api/orders/{orderId} returns any order by id with no owner filter (OrderQueries.cs:8-10). POST / takes UserId, UserName, address and card data from the request body rather than the token sub (OrdersApi.cs:118-185; the identity service exists but is not used there). evidence.statement: The paymentmethods table maps CardHolderName (max 200), Alias, CardNumber (required, max 25), Expiration and CardTypeId from private fields. PaymentMethod keeps _securityNumber as a private field set in the constructor; the entity configuration maps no column for it, and a text search of Ordering.Domain, Ordering.Infrastructure and Ordering.API for 'securitynumber' found only constructor, command, domain-event and request-record plumbing, no mapping or repository write. The orders table maps OrderStatus as a string (max 30), owns the Address value object (street, city, state, zip, country) and links PaymentMethodId and BuyerId. evidence.statement: GetSubscriptionsOfType returns every subscription of the event type (db.Subscriptions.Where(s => s.Type == type)) with no UserId or order-owner predicate. The Paid and Shipped handlers pass that full list with a WebhookData built by serializing the received event to JSON to WebhooksSender.SendAll. Webhooks.API's own event records carry OrderId and OrderStockItems (ProductId, Units) for Paid, and OrderId, OrderStatus and BuyerName for Shipped. Ordering.API's published Paid event also carries BuyerIdentityGuid, which Webhooks.API's record does not declare. Delivery is therefore to all subscribers of a type, for any user's order.
evidence.limitations: WebhookData.cs seen through search context (lines 1-16); WebhooksSender internals were read at collection (E11). The per-subscription Token header handling on delivery was not re-read.

evidence.statement: LoggingBehavior logs every command with the {@Command} destructuring operator before and after the handler, and the response. ValidatorBehavior logs the command and the validation failures when validation fails. TransactionBehavior opens a database transaction, logs the command at begin and on error, commits, and only then publishes integration events (PublishEventsThroughEventBusAsync(transactionId)) inside the execution strategy. CreateOrderCommand exposes CardNumber, CardHolderName, CardExpiration and CardSecurityNumber as [DataMember] properties with no log-exclusion attribute seen. Validators: Create checks required address fields, card number length 12-19, security number length 3, future expiry and at least one item; Cancel and Ship check only that OrderNumber is non-empty. RequestManager.CreateRequestForCommandAsync saves a ClientRequest (Id, Name = command type name, Time) and throws if the id already exists; the record carries no user or payload binding.
evidence.limitations: Behavior registration order and whether RequestManager's SaveChanges falls inside TransactionBehavior's transaction were not read (G8). How {@Command} is rendered depends on the logging provider, which was not observed (G-s01-log-sinks). IdentifiedCommandValidator was not read.

evidence.statement: Order is created with OrderStatus.Submitted (constructor, line 57). SetAwaitingValidationStatus acts only from Submitted; SetStockConfirmedStatus only from AwaitingValidation; SetPaidStatus only from StockConfirmed; each is a silent no-op from any other state. SetShippedStatus throws unless the status is Paid. SetCancelledStatus throws only from Paid or Shipped, so it succeeds from Submitted, AwaitingValidation, StockConfirmed and also from Cancelled (raising OrderCancelledDomainEvent again). SetCancelledStatusWhenStockIsRejected acts only from AwaitingValidation. The Paid description reads as a simulated bank account. Order state changes raise domain events that become integration events.
evidence.limitations: Domain model read in full; the callers (command handlers and integration event handlers) are covered by E7, E9, E12 and unread handler bodies (G-s01-event-handlers).

evidence.statement: The four Ordering consumers act on the OrderId in the event alone and send a plain (not Identified) command: GracePeriodConfirmed to SetAwaitingValidation, OrderStockConfirmed to SetStockConfirmed, OrderPaymentSucceeded to SetPaid, OrderPaymentFailed to CancelOrderCommand. They check no sender identity, user, amount or other correlation. The Set* handlers wait 10 seconds (Task.Delay) and then load the order by number and call the aggregate transition; a missing order returns false. Each consumer logs the whole event and the command.
evidence.limitations: SetAwaitingValidation and SetStockRejected handlers, the order repository and mediator pipeline order were not read; behaviour of the aggregate on a wrong-state call is from E31.

evidence.statement: On AwaitingValidation, Catalog compares AvailableStock with the units in the event for each ProductId and publishes OrderStockConfirmed or OrderStockRejected; it reserves nothing. On the Paid event it calls RemoveStock(Units) for each item in the event ('we're not blocking stock/inventory'), without checking that the order exists, was seen before, or that the event id is new, then saves.
evidence.limitations: RemoveStock semantics (for example a throw on insufficient stock), CatalogIntegrationEventService and the publish retry were not read.

evidence.statement: OnMessageReceived always acknowledges the delivery, including after an exception (comment: a dead-letter exchange belongs in a real app), so a failed handler loses the message. A message body containing the text 'throw-fake-exception' forces an exception before processing. The full body is written to the warning log on error and set as the activity tag 'message' on every receive. Unknown routing keys log a warning and return; known keys deserialize into the statically registered type and run each handler in sequence.
evidence.limitations: Lines 90-240 read in this stage plus earlier grep and selected lines (IN-061); prefetch, concurrency and reconnect logic unread.

evidence.statement: The picture endpoint finds the item, takes PictureFileName, calls GetFileInfo on a keyed PhysicalFileProvider rooted at ContentRoot/Pics and streams the file with a content type chosen from the extension. The code adds no normalisation or allow-list of its own; confinement to Pics rests on the provider. No upload route was seen in the lines read.
evidence.limitations: CatalogApi.cs read in ranges only (IN-057); provider behaviour for rooted or parent-relative names is framework behaviour, not observed or tested here.

evidence.statement: Delivery builds a POST to the stored DestUrl with the serialized WebhookData and, when the subscription has a Token, adds it as header X-eshop-whtoken. It uses the default IHttpClientFactory client, awaits Task.WhenAll over all receivers, never inspects the response and sets no timeout, redirect or address policy in code.
evidence.limitations: Default handler redirect and timeout behaviour is framework behaviour, not observed; egress policy unobserved (UB4).

evidence.statement: Token is optional: validation checks only that Url and GrantUrl are well formed and Event parses. With an empty Token the expected value becomes null, and an OPTIONS response with a 2xx status and no X-eshop-whtoken header satisfies the check (null equals null), so no echo is needed. The same-origin test compares scheme, port and host strings, not resolved addresses. The grant check logs the token, the received token and the expected token; the failure response echoes the GrantUrl to the caller.
evidence.limitations: Reading shows the logic; no request was sent. Whether a given internal target answers OPTIONS with 2xx is unobserved.

evidence.statement: Create builds order items from the request body (product id, name, unit price, discount, units) with no catalog or price lookup in the handler; the OrderStartedIntegrationEvent is built from the body UserId and saved before the order is created. CreateOrderAsync returns 200 OK whether the command result is true or false (the result is only logged). Cancel and ship log the command and request id only; no principal is logged or stored in the code read. The x-requestid header is a Guid chosen by the caller.
evidence.limitations: Lines read in the ranges named; BasketItem and the aggregate item constructor were not read; log rendering depends on the provider (G-s01-log-sinks).

evidence.statement: Re-read in full by stage 03. WithExternalHttpEndpoints is applied to identity-api, the mobile-bff YARP resource and webapp only. webhooks-api has no external endpoint and is referenced only by the webhooksclient sample (WithReference at line 68); webapp references basket-api, catalog-api and ordering-api but not webhooks-api. Identity__Url is passed to basket-api, ordering-api and webhooks-api and not to catalog-api. Embedding and chat models are wired only inside the opt-in AddFoundry (UseFoundry configuration flag) and AddOllama (useOllama local variable set to false) branches.
evidence.limitations: Configuration observation; deployed topology and ACA ingress not observed (G1). Consistent with E1, E2 and E18; not independent corroboration of them.

evidence.statement: Re-read in full by stage 03. ConfigureMobileBffRoutes defines routes for the explicit /catalog-api/api/catalog/... paths (items, items/{id}, items/by, pic, brands, types and search variants), the catch-all /api/catalog/{*any}, /api/orders/{*any} and /identity/{*any}. No route sets a method match, an authorization policy or a request header transform; the only transform is path-prefix removal. Catalog and orders routes require an exact api-version query value (catalog 1.0, 1 or 2.0; orders 1.0 or 1). No route targets basket-api or webhooks-api. AddForwardedHeaders only adds the ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED environment variable to DotnetProject resources.
evidence.limitations: Configuration read only; the YARP configuration actually generated and loaded by the gateway is unobserved (G2, UB1). Whether YARP copies the Authorization header by default is framework behavior, not observed here.

evidence.locator: src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:1-130,245-468; src/Catalog.API/Program.cs:1-29; text search of src for AddDefaultAuthentication, UseAuthentication, UseAuthorization, Authorize, RequireAuthorization, AllowAnonymous
evidence.statement: A text search over all of Catalog.API found no authentication registration, no Authorize attribute and no RequireAuthorization; AddDefaultAuthentication appears only in the Basket, Ordering and Webhooks extensions. Catalog Program.cs calls no UseAuthentication or UseAuthorization. Write routes: PUT /items (version 1.0, id in body), PUT /items/{id} (version 2.0), POST /items and DELETE /items/{id} (versions 1.0 and 2.0), all inside the api-version values the gateway routes accept (E40). UpdateItem copies the whole request body onto the entity with SetValues; CreateItem keeps a client-supplied Id and PictureFileName. The picture route passes PictureFileName to the keyed provider and returns octet-stream for unknown extensions.
evidence.limitations: CatalogApi.cs lines 131-244 were not re-read in this stage; text search proves only the matched lines. Not independent of E4 and E35 for the route behavior.

evidence.statement: RemoveStock throws CatalogDomainException when AvailableStock is 0 or the requested units are 0 or less; otherwise it removes the smaller of requested units and available stock, so stock never goes below zero. The Paid handler loops over the event items, calls RemoveStock on each found item and calls SaveChangesAsync once after the loop; an exception in one item skips the remaining items and the save. The handler checks no order id and no event id.
evidence.limitations: CatalogItem.cs read only as search context around RemoveStock and AddStock (about lines 62-92); remainder unread. Extends E33.

evidence.statement: Read in full. IsEnabled is true only when an IEmbeddingGenerator was registered. The embedding input is Name plus a space plus Description with no length limit in this code. When disabled, GetEmbeddingAsync(item) returns null, so UpdateItem stores a null embedding. Embeddings are cut to 384 dimensions.
evidence.limitations: Registration of the generator was read only through the AppHost wiring (E39); provider behavior and any provider-side limits are unobserved (UB3).

evidence.statement: MediatR registers the open behaviors Logging, Validator and Transaction for every request, so an IdentifiedCommand runs inside TransactionBehavior's transaction. IdentifiedCommandHandler calls RequestManager.CreateRequestForCommandAsync, which saves the ClientRequest through SaveChangesAsync on the same scoped OrderingContext, then sends the inner command inside try/catch with catch { return default; }. An exception from the inner command therefore never reaches TransactionBehavior, which commits and publishes events; the stored request id survives and the result is false. IdentifiedCommandValidator checks only that the id is non-empty. The handler logs the inner command with {@Command} before and after it runs.
evidence.limitations: Reading shows control flow; no request was sent. Behavior when the database itself fails inside the inner command (an aborted PostgreSQL transaction) is runtime behavior not observed. Extends E9 and E30; the same files are partly cited there.

evidence.statement: CancelOrderAsync and ShipOrderAsync return a 500 problem when the identified command returns false; CreateOrderAsync returns 200 OK in both cases. The cancel, ship and create identified handlers all return true for a duplicate request id (CreateResultForDuplicateRequest). The cancel handler calls the aggregate's SetCancelledStatus, which throws from Paid or Shipped; the exception is swallowed (E44) so the route reports 500 on the first attempt and a retry with the same id reports 200. CreateOrderAsync never reads the token subject; the create validator has no rule on UserId. GET by id catches any exception and returns 404.
evidence.limitations: Ship and create handler files read only as search context for the duplicate-result method. Extends E7, E38 and E44; not independent of them for the route behavior.

evidence.statement: Assistant and user messages are rendered through MessageProcessor.AllowImages. Message text is HTML-encoded, but markdown image syntax is converted to an img element whose src is the HTML-attribute-encoded URL taken from the message with no scheme or host allow-list. A model reply can therefore make the browser request an arbitrary URL.
evidence.limitations: Chatbot.razor read only through search matches. A Content-Security-Policy or other header that blocks external images was not read (G10). Active only when a chat model is configured.

evidence.locator: src/Basket.API/appsettings.json:17-19; src/Ordering.API/appsettings.json:29-33; src/Webhooks.API/appsettings.json:29-33; src/Catalog.API/appsettings.json (text search, no match)
evidence.statement: Basket.API, Ordering.API and Webhooks.API each define an Identity section with an Audience (basket, orders, webhooks); Webhooks.API also holds a placeholder localhost Url that AppHost overrides. A text search of Catalog.API appsettings.json for an Identity section found none. Section presence makes AddDefaultAuthentication register JwtBearer (E6).
evidence.limitations: Read as matched lines only; deployed configuration overrides are unobserved (G4).

evidence.statement: UseDefaultOpenApi does nothing unless an OpenApi configuration section exists. When it does, the OpenAPI document endpoint is mapped in every environment, and the Scalar API reference UI plus a redirect from / to it are mapped only when the environment is Development. OpenApiOptionsExtensions defines an OAuth2 security scheme with an implicit flow (search match lines only).
evidence.limitations: OpenApiOptionsExtensions.cs not opened; which Identity.API client the scheme uses and the redirect URIs were not read (G5, G10). Whether each service sets the OpenApi section was not checked.

evidence.locator: src/Identity.API/Program.cs:1-57; src/Identity.API/Quickstart/Account/AccountController.cs:70-135; text search of Identity.API (.cs and .cshtml) for lockout, register and password-option terms
evidence.statement: The login action calls PasswordSignInAsync with lockoutOnFailure true and validates return URLs. Program.cs calls AddMigration with UsersSeed with no environment condition and registers no password or lockout options (framework defaults apply). The only registration-related matches are a RegisterViewModel record; no register action or view was found by search. AddDeveloperSigningCredential and disabled key management are confirmed (E15).
evidence.limitations: AccountController read to line 135 plus search matches only; views and other controllers unread (G10, G11); lockout defaults are framework behavior, not observed. Search proves only matched lines. UsersSeed.cs was not re-read.

evidence.statement: SetAwaitingValidation loads the order by number and calls SetAwaitingValidationStatus with no delay. SetStockRejected waits 10 seconds, loads the order and calls SetCancelledStatusWhenStockIsRejected. The OrderStockRejected consumer builds the command from the event OrderId and the items without stock; no sender, user or amount is checked. No handler issues a refund, void or compensating event.
evidence.limitations: Aggregate guards are from E31. Behavior of the mediator pipeline for these non-identified commands follows E44 only by registration order. Extends E32.

evidence.statement: Every CheckUpdateTime (30 seconds) the service queries ordering.orders for ids whose status is Submitted and whose age is at least GracePeriodTime (1 minute) and publishes a GracePeriodConfirmed event for each, repeatedly until the order leaves Submitted. A database error returns an empty list. No query or job selects orders left in AwaitingValidation or StockConfirmed.
evidence.limitations: Only this service was read as a re-driver; other jobs, broker redelivery settings and outbox republish (G-s03-outbox-redelivery) were not read. Extends E20.

states.description: Grace window: a time condition on Submitted orders. OrderProcessor polls every 30 seconds with a 1 minute grace period and publishes GracePeriodConfirmed. Cancel through the API is not blocked during this window. The selection query body was not read.

states.description: AwaitingValidation: Submitted moves here through SetAwaitingValidationStatus, expected on GracePeriodConfirmed; Ordering's handler was not read. Stock rejection moves it to Cancelled.

threats.scenario: Catalog.API registers no authentication and maps PUT items, PUT items/{id}, POST items and DELETE items/{id} without RequireAuthorization. Any caller that can send HTTP to catalog-api can create, rewrite (price, description, picture name, stock fields in the body) or delete items. Internet reach would come through the mobile-bff catch-all /api/catalog/{*any}, which shows no method restriction; reach from inside the environment needs only a foothold on any workload.
threats.objective: Integrity and availability of product, price and description data.
prerequisites: A request reaches catalog-api: through the YARP catch-all with PUT, POST or DELETE passed, or from a foothold inside Z-internal
Target ids are guessable or listed through the read routes
actor_assumptions: Unauthenticated internet client, or a low-privilege workload inside the environment
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: E4 shows the write routes and a search of the service found no authentication registration; E3 shows a catch-all with no method match. Against: E2 shows no external endpoint for catalog-api, and the effective YARP and ACA configuration is unobserved, so internet reach is unconfirmed. Observation that would decide it: generated YARP configuration or one PUT through the gateway. Stage 03 counterexample search: E41 extends the search for any authentication or authorization registration to all of Catalog.API and found none, and AppHost passes no Identity__Url to catalog-api (E39). E40 shows every mobile-bff route, including the explicit /catalog-api/api/catalog/items and items/{id} routes and the catch-all, with no method match, authorization policy or header transform, and the write routes' api-version values (1.0 or 2.0) fall inside the values the routes accept. No protective control on the write path was found. Internet reach is still unconfirmed because the generated gateway and ACA ingress are unobserved, so confidence stays medium.

threats.scenario: Using the unauthenticated update route, a caller changes an item Price. Catalog recomputes the embedding and publishes ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent, so the altered price reaches the storefront and the bus. The only consumer read, Webhooks.API, ignores the event. Ordering takes unit price from the order request body, so the catalog price is not what an order records.
threats.objective: Correctness of displayed prices and of price-change notifications.

Against: stage 03 read CatalogAI (E43): an embedding exists only when an embedding generator is registered, which AppHost does only in the opt-in Foundry or Ollama branches (E39); otherwise update stores a null embedding, so the ranking-steering premise fails in the default deployment. The text change itself still reaches the storefront and the chat tools (tm02:T-chat-indirect-injection-addtocart). Provider behavior is unobserved (UB3). Narrowed in stage 03; confidence stays low.

threats.scenario: When a chat model is configured, SearchCatalog returns catalog descriptions to the model. A description written through the unauthenticated update route, or text typed by the customer, can carry instructions. The model can then call AddToCart and GetCartContents, which run with the signed-in user's token against Basket, without a per-call confirmation seen in the code.
threats.objective: Integrity of the customer's basket and of actions taken in their name.
prerequisites: Chat is enabled (Foundry opt-in or Ollama flag, both off by default per E18)
Attacker can place text in catalog data or the chat
Model follows embedded instructions
actor_assumptions: Catalog write caller or the customer themselves
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: untrusted text reaches a model with executable tools (E18). Against: chat needs a model connection that is not configured by default; the tools touch only a cart under the user's own subject, and the checkout step is a separate user action (not read). Model behaviour is unobserved (UB3).

threats.scenario: The GetUserInfo tool returns name, address, email and phone from the signed-in user's claims to the model. Injected instructions (catalog text or a hostile page the user pastes) can ask the model to repeat that data in its reply or pass it to the provider's logs. Provider handling and output rendering are not read.
threats.objective: Confidentiality of the customer's contact data.
prerequisites: Chat is enabled
Instructions reach the model
Reply content reaches an attacker: the reply is readable by them, the browser requests a model-supplied image URL (no URL allow-list in the rendering code, E46), or the provider logs the data
actor_assumptions: Catalog write caller, or a customer pasting hostile text
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: the tool returns PII to the model (E18), and stage 03 read the rendering path (E46): message text is HTML-encoded, but markdown image syntax becomes an img element whose src is the model-supplied URL with no allow-list, so a model that follows injected instructions can place user data in a URL the browser requests. Against: chat needs a model connection that is off by default (E18, E39); whether a model follows injected instructions is unobserved (UB3); a Content-Security-Policy that blocks external images was not read (G10); the data is the signed-in user's own. The rendering premise is now observed, the others are not, so confidence stays low.

threats.scenario: PictureFileName is client-writable through the update and create routes and is passed to a PhysicalFileProvider rooted at Pics. If the provider accepted a rooted or parent-relative name, the endpoint could stream a file outside Pics.
threats.objective: Confidentiality of files on the Catalog.API host.
prerequisites: tm02:T-catalog-unauth-write holds
The provider does not confine the name (not shown)
actor_assumptions: Same as the catalog write caller
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: the stored name reaches the provider unchanged (E35). Against: the file store is a rooted provider, the latest commit message in session context claims a confinement fix, and no upload route was seen, so the realistic effect is selecting among existing Pics files. Unconfirmed protection, so a gap is linked.

threats.scenario: Any caller holding a token the Ordering service accepts calls GET api/orders/{orderId} with another customer's integer id. The query has no owner filter and returns that order (address, items, status).
threats.objective: Confidentiality of other customers' order and address data.
prerequisites: Attacker holds an Identity-issued token (see tm02:T-seeded-users-known-credentials, tm02:T-jwt-audience-scopeless-cross-api)
Attacker reaches Ordering's HTTP API directly: through the /api/orders YARP route or from inside the environment
Order ids are small integers and can be enumerated
actor_assumptions: Authenticated customer or any holder of a valid token
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: E7 states by-id read has no owner filter (OrderQueries read in full). Against: WebApp pages show only the caller's own orders, and reaching the API directly depends on the BFF route forwarding the bearer token (G-s01-bff-auth-forwarding) or an internal foothold. No stated ownership rule exists (GAP-invariants). Stage 03: E45 re-read of the route confirms no owner comparison. AppHost declares /api/orders/{*any} on the external mobile-bff with no method, policy or header transform (E40), and Ordering has an Identity section so authentication is registered (E47). Whether the gateway forwards the bearer token and whether the generated ingress matches the declaration remain unobserved (G-s01-bff-auth-forwarding, G1, G2); confidence stays medium.

threats.scenario: Any authenticated caller sends PUT cancel or PUT ship with another order's number. Neither checks owner, role or scope (a comment says an administrator ships). Cancel works from Submitted, AwaitingValidation, StockConfirmed and repeats from Cancelled; ship works on any Paid order and starts the Shipped webhook fan-out.
threats.objective: Integrity of order fulfilment and customer commitments.
prerequisites: Attacker holds an accepted token
Attacker reaches Ordering's HTTP API
Target order number is known or enumerated (see tm02:T-orders-read-any-order)
actor_assumptions: Authenticated customer
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: E7 shows no owner or role check; E31 shows which states allow cancel and ship. Against: state guards stop cancel after Paid and ship before Paid (C-order-state-guards); reach depends on the same BFF and ingress unknowns. No role or scope exists in the identity configuration to check against (E14). Stage 03: cancel and ship return a 500 when the inner command fails (E45), so a blocked attempt is visible to the caller; the aggregate state guards (E31) remain the only protection and no owner or role check exists on either route. Reach is as for tm02:T-orders-read-any-order (E40, E47). Confidence stays medium.

threats.scenario: POST api/orders takes UserId, UserName and Buyer from the body. A caller sets UserId to a victim's subject. Ordering builds the OrderStartedIntegrationEvent from that body UserId, and Basket.API deletes the basket for that id. The order is also recorded against the victim. POST draft takes a client BuyerId in the same way.
threats.objective: Integrity of another customer's basket and of order attribution.
prerequisites: Attacker holds an accepted token and reaches Ordering's HTTP API
Victim subject id is known (Identity subjects are GUIDs; how an attacker learns one is not shown)
actor_assumptions: Authenticated customer
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: body-supplied UserId is observed (E7, E38) and the Basket handler deletes by the event's UserId (E20). Against: subject ids are not guessable and no source of them was found; Basket itself keys by token subject only (C-basket-sub-keying), so direct basket access stays protected. Stage 03: the create validator has no rule on UserId, IdentifiedCommandValidator checks only the request id (E44, E45), and the route never reads the token subject, so nothing ties the body UserId to the caller. The source of a victim's subject id is still not shown; confidence stays medium.

threats.scenario: Order creation adds items using the unit price, discount and name from the request body with no catalog lookup. An authenticated caller can record an order at any price. Payment is simulated in this system, so no money is charged; if a real gateway were added, the recorded amount would be caller-controlled.
threats.objective: Integrity of order totals.
prerequisites: Attacker holds an accepted token and reaches the Ordering API directly (WebApp builds items from its own basket)
actor_assumptions: Authenticated customer
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: E38 shows body-supplied price; E30 shows validators check counts and card fields only. Against: payment is simulated (E20), so there is no financial effect in the code as shipped. Whether a downstream process re-prices is not shown.

threats.scenario: Order create is wrapped in an IdentifiedCommand keyed by the caller-chosen x-requestid. The id is saved before the inner command, and the handler swallows any exception from the inner command, so the surrounding transaction commits with the id stored. CreateOrderAsync then returns 200 OK whether the command succeeded or not. After a failed first attempt (for example a domain exception), a retry with the same id gets a canned success and never runs, so the customer sees success for an order that does not exist. This threat covers create only: cancel and ship report failure as a 500 (see tm03:T-orders-cancel-ship-retry-reports-success).
threats.objective: Correct outcome of an order submission across a retry.
prerequisites: First attempt fails after the id is saved (for example a database error)
Client retries with the same x-requestid
actor_assumptions: Customer client retrying; no attacker needed
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: E9 and E44 show the id is saved on the same scoped context inside TransactionBehavior's transaction and the inner exception never reaches the behavior, so the commit keeps the id; E38 and E45 show the route answers OK regardless. Against: the earlier open question was whether the save rolls back with the failed command; stage 03 read the behavior order (Logging, Validator, Transaction) and the handler, which contradicts rollback for exceptions raised in the inner command. A database error that aborts the PostgreSQL transaction could make the commit fail and release the id, which is runtime behavior not observed (G8). Clients may not retry with the same id; WebApp ordering code is unread (UN-005). Confidence stays medium.

threats.scenario: Cancel, ship and create log the command and request id but no calling principal, and the ClientRequest row holds no user. After a disputed cancellation, ship or order, the code read cannot say which authenticated user did it.
threats.objective: Accountability for order state changes.
prerequisites: Log sinks and any gateway or identity logs carry the actor (not observed)
actor_assumptions: Any authenticated user later denying an action
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: E38 and E30 show no principal in the logged commands or the request record. Against: gateway, platform or Identity logs may record the caller; log sinks are unobserved (G-s01-log-sinks).

threats.scenario: Basket, Ordering and Webhooks share one JWT configuration with ValidateAudience false and no scope or role policy. A token minted for one API or client (for example the basket-only Swagger client, or a client with no API scope) is accepted by the others, because issuer, signature and lifetime are all that is checked.
threats.objective: Separation between APIs and between granted scopes.
prerequisites: Attacker holds any access token signed by Identity.API with an accepted issuer
Identity section present in the target service (G4)
actor_assumptions: Holder of a token meant for a narrower purpose
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: E6 shows audience validation off and a default-only authorization setup; E14 shows scopes per client that the services never test. Against: signature, issuer and lifetime are still enforced (C-jwt-validation) and a token needs a real login or client grant. Effective per-service configuration is unobserved. Stage 03: Basket, Ordering and Webhooks each carry an Identity section with an Audience in appsettings.json and AppHost passes Identity__Url to them (E47, E39), so authentication is registered in each at source level; Catalog has none (E41). This narrows the G4 premise to deployed-configuration overrides; confidence stays medium.

threats.scenario: The webapp, webhooksclient and one more confidential registration share one literal sample secret, and webapp does not require PKCE. The maui app ships a secret constant although it is a public client. If these values are deployed unchanged, a party who intercepts an authorization code for webapp can redeem it as that client; any holder of the sample secret can act as a confidential client at the token endpoint.
threats.objective: Confidentiality of authorization codes and tokens; integrity of client authentication.
prerequisites: Sample secrets are unchanged in the deployed configuration
Attacker can capture an authorization code (redirect or log leak, device malware)
actor_assumptions: Network or device-level attacker with a captured code
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: E14 and E17 show shared literal secrets and RequirePkce false for webapp; E24 shows the maui secret in app code. Against: code capture is a separate prerequisite, maui requires PKCE (C-maui-pkce), redirect and return-URL checks exist (C-identity-csrf-redirect) and Identity controllers are read by grep only (G10).

threats.scenario: Three implicit-flow clients (basket, ordering and webhooks Swagger UI) return access tokens to the browser (AllowAccessTokensViaBrowser). Tokens in the URL fragment can leak through history, extensions or a redirect to an unintended registered URI; tokens are accepted by every API (tm02:T-jwt-audience-scopeless-cross-api).
threats.objective: Confidentiality of browser-delivered access tokens.
prerequisites: Clients are registered in the deployed Identity.API (they are in Config.cs regardless of environment)
A victim signs in through a Swagger page or an attacker controls a registered redirect
actor_assumptions: Attacker with access to a victim's browser context
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: implicit clients with browser-delivered tokens are registered (E14). Against: redirect URIs and whether Swagger UI is enabled outside development were not read. Stage 03: the in-service API reference UI is mapped only in the Development environment and only when an OpenApi section exists (E48), so the pages that would drive these implicit clients are not mapped in a non-Development deployment; the client registrations stay in Identity.API in every environment (E14). The remaining exposure is a request crafted by anyone against the implicit clients' registered redirect URIs, which were not re-read. Confidence stays low.

threats.scenario: Identity.API runs with AddDeveloperSigningCredential and key management disabled, both commented as not for production. Anyone who can read the stored developer key can sign tokens that every resource service accepts; a redeploy or several replicas can also change or split the key.
threats.objective: Integrity of tokens issued by Identity.API.
prerequisites: Attacker reads the key from the Identity.API file system, image or backup, or code-level access to the host
Issuer value matches an accepted issuer
actor_assumptions: Attacker with read access to the Identity.API workload storage
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: developer credential and disabled key management are observed (E15). Against: key location and access are unobserved and no key file was opened; resource services also check the issuer.

threats.scenario: Identity.API creates users alice and bob with one sample password at every startup, in any environment, with profile data and card details. An internet client signs in at the externally exposed Identity.API with the published password and holds a real customer session, which is the prerequisite for the order, webhook and JWT scenarios.
threats.objective: Confidentiality and integrity of customer accounts and the authenticated attack surface.
prerequisites: Seed ran in the deployed environment and the sample password is unchanged
Identity.API reachable (it declares an external endpoint)
actor_assumptions: Unauthenticated internet client who has read the repository
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: seed runs on every startup (E16) and Identity.API is external (E2). Against: README says the deployment is for evaluation and demonstrations (E26); lockout, rate limiting and any deployment override are unobserved (G-s02-account-provisioning). Stage 03: the login action uses lockoutOnFailure true and no registration action or view was found by search (E49), so seeded accounts are the only account source seen; lockout does not limit a correct published password, and Program.cs seeds with no environment condition (E49). How non-seed accounts arise stays open. Confidence stays medium.

threats.scenario: An authenticated caller registers a webhook with Url and GrantUrl pointing at an internal host and port and leaves Token empty. The grant check then passes when that host answers OPTIONS with any 2xx and no token header, so no cooperation from the target is needed. Webhooks.API sends the OPTIONS request itself, and later POSTs each Paid or Shipped payload to Url with a caller-chosen header. A host the attacker controls can also pass the check and later redirect or re-resolve to an internal address.
threats.objective: Integrity of Z-internal as a network boundary; use of Webhooks.API as an egress proxy.
prerequisites: Attacker holds an accepted token and can reach Webhooks.API's registration route (no external endpoint and no gateway route is declared, so the path is unknown, G1)
Target answers OPTIONS with 2xx, or the attacker's host passes and then redirects or re-resolves
No egress filtering
actor_assumptions: Holder of an Identity-issued token who can reach the Webhooks.API registration route; AppHost declares no customer path to webhooks-api (E39, E40)
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: E37 shows token optional and a null-equals-null pass, same-origin check on strings only, no address block; E36 shows delivery with no response handling. Against: the registration route may not be reachable by customers (G1), the POST body is fixed event JSON rather than attacker bytes, and egress policy is unobserved (UB4). The handshake still stops targets that answer non-2xx. Stage 03 downgrade from medium to low: AppHost declares no customer path to webhooks-api. It has no external endpoint, no mobile-bff route targets it and WebApp does not reference it; only the internal WebhookClient sample does (E39, E40, E2), so reach needs an internal foothold or an ingress that differs from the declaration (G1). The re-read handshake logic still shows the empty-token pass (E37). The OPTIONS request goes to any well-formed same-origin target before any outcome check, and the caller sees only a 201 or a 400 echoing the GrantUrl, so the primary effect is a blind request and a reachability signal, not a response read.

threats.scenario: Webhooks.API sends every Paid and Shipped event to all subscriptions of that type with no owner filter. A customer who registers a subscription receives the order id, product units (Paid) and buyer name (Shipped) for other customers' orders. Any customer can also trigger Shipped deliveries through tm02:T-orders-cancel-ship-any-order.
threats.objective: Confidentiality of other customers' order identifiers and buyer names.
prerequisites: Attacker registers a subscription (needs a token and the registration route, G1)
Orders reach Paid or Shipped
actor_assumptions: Authenticated customer with a webhook receiver
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: E29 shows the retriever selects by type only. Against: list, get and delete are owner-scoped (C-webhook-owner-scope) and the registration route's reachability is unknown (G1); payload fields are limited to identifiers, units and buyer name. Stage 03 downgrade from medium to low for the reach premise: who can register a subscription is open because AppHost declares no customer path to webhooks-api (no external endpoint, no gateway route, no WebApp reference; E39, E40), so a cross-user receiver needs the registration route to be reachable (G1). The missing owner predicate in the retriever is unchanged (E29).

threats.scenario: The grant check logs the caller's token, the token received and the token expected, and WebhookClient logs the received and expected tokens. Subscription tokens are sent in plain header text on each delivery. WebhookClient's /webhook-received and /check endpoints are unauthenticated and validate the token only if ValidateToken is on (default off). Log readers obtain tokens; anyone reaching a sample receiver can inject fake notifications.
threats.objective: Confidentiality of webhook tokens; authenticity of webhook notifications at the sample receiver.
prerequisites: Attacker reads logs (sinks unobserved) or reaches the sample receiver
ValidateToken is off or the token leaks
actor_assumptions: Log reader, or any network peer of WebhookClient
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: token logging is directly observed (E11, E13, E37) and the sample receiver is open (E13). Against: the token is a per-subscription proof value rather than a user credential, WebhookClient is a sample with no external endpoint (E2), and log access is unobserved.

threats.scenario: Any holder of the shared broker credential publishes OrderStockConfirmed, OrderPaymentSucceeded, OrderPaymentFailed or OrderStockRejected with a chosen OrderId. A forged GracePeriodConfirmed only skips a wait of about one minute, because the order processor re-publishes it for every order still Submitted (E51). Ordering applies each event to the named order using only that id, guarded by the aggregate state (E31): StockConfirmed moves AwaitingValidation to StockConfirmed and skips the real stock check; PaymentSucceeded moves StockConfirmed to Paid; PaymentFailed cancels from Submitted, AwaitingValidation or StockConfirmed; StockRejected cancels from AwaitingValidation. A Paid order can then be shipped by any authenticated user (tm02:T-orders-cancel-ship-any-order).
threats.objective: Integrity of order state and the payment and stock steps.
prerequisites: Attacker publishes to the exchange: a compromised workload that holds the injected credential, or an exposed broker
Target OrderId known (integer, see tm02:T-orders-read-any-order)
actor_assumptions: Low-privilege workload or any holder of the broker credential
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: events carry no signature or sender identity (E19), consumers trust the OrderId alone (E32). Against: the aggregate guards transitions and treats a wrong-state call as a no-op or throw (C-order-state-guards), unknown event types are dropped (tm02:C-bus-unknown-type-drop), and broker users, vhosts and network exposure are unobserved (UB2, G3). Service compromise is an assumed prerequisite, not an observed incident. Stage 03: payment success is already unconditional in PaymentProcessor (E20), so a forged success adds little beyond skipping the stock check; targeted cancellation through forged failure or rejection and the stock-check bypass are the distinct effects. The AwaitingValidation and StockRejected handlers were read and also act on the OrderId alone (E50). Broker access remains an assumed prerequisite; confidence stays medium.

threats.scenario: A forged OrderStatusChangedToPaid event with chosen ProductIds and Units makes Catalog remove that stock for orders that do not exist, and a replayed genuine Paid event removes stock again because no event id or order check is made. RemoveStock clamps at the available quantity and throws for zero stock or non-positive units, so stock can be driven to zero but not below, and an item that throws aborts the rest of the loop before the save (E42). Fabricated Paid or Shipped content reaching webhook subscribers is split out into tm03:T-bus-forged-paid-shipped-webhook-content.
threats.objective: Integrity of stock levels.
prerequisites: Attacker can publish to the exchange, or a genuine event is redelivered (no dead letter or replay protection was seen)
RemoveStock accepts the quantities (unread)
actor_assumptions: Low-privilege workload or any holder of the broker credential
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: Catalog handler acts on event fields without an order lookup (E33) and RemoveStock accepts any positive quantity up to the available stock (E42). Against: broker access is a prerequisite (UB2); replay by genuine redelivery would need an unacked delivery to be redelivered, but the consumer acknowledges every message (E34) and outbox republish behavior is unread (G-s03-outbox-redelivery), so the replay branch is weaker than the forged branch; stock is not reserved before payment, so oversell exists without an attacker. Split in stage 03: the webhook-content effect has a different recipient and evidence and is now its own threat. Confidence stays medium.

threats.scenario: A forged OrderStartedIntegrationEvent naming a UserId makes Basket.API delete that user's basket. The same event is produced from an order create request that carries a chosen UserId (tm02:T-orders-create-foreign-userid), so broker access is not the only route.
threats.objective: Availability of a customer's basket contents.
prerequisites: Attacker publishes to the exchange, or uses the Ordering create route
Victim UserId known
actor_assumptions: Holder of the broker credential, or authenticated customer
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: Basket deletes by the event's UserId (E20). Against: impact is loss of a cart, ids are not guessable and no source of ids was found.

threats.scenario: The consumer acknowledges every message, including after an exception, with no retry or dead-letter path, and the handlers of one event run in sequence so an exception in one skips the later ones. A transient failure while handling stock or payment events permanently loses that step and leaves the order in AwaitingValidation or StockConfirmed with no timeout or re-driver seen. The first step is recovered: the order processor re-publishes GracePeriodConfirmed every 30 seconds for each order still Submitted past the grace period (E51), and SetAwaitingValidation ignores repeats because the aggregate acts only from Submitted (E31). A message containing 'throw-fake-exception' is forced to fail the same way.
threats.objective: Completion and consistency of the order workflow after a partial failure.
prerequisites: A handler throws (database error, timeout) or a crafted body is published
No reconciler restarts the order (none read)
actor_assumptions: No attacker needed; a publisher can induce it with a crafted body
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: E34 shows always-ack and the failure trigger; E32 shows handlers that can fail (database load and save). Against: ordering uses an outbox for publish (C-transactional-publish) and a reconciler may exist outside what was read (G-s01-retry-recovery). Whether the outcome is unknown or failed to the customer is not shown. Stage 03 counterexample: the Submitted to AwaitingValidation step self-heals (E51), so a lost GracePeriodConfirmed is not stuck. No equivalent re-driver was found for AwaitingValidation or StockConfirmed, and a failed Paid handling in Catalog is not retried. Repeated GracePeriodConfirmed delivery is a repeated transport delivery without a repeated business effect, unlike the Catalog Paid handler (E42). The threat is narrowed to the later steps; confidence stays medium.

threats.scenario: Event bodies are written to the error log and attached to every receive span; handlers log whole events and commands; the create route logs IdentifiedCommand<CreateOrderCommand> with {@Command}, and CreateOrderCommand carries CardSecurityNumber, holder name and expiry. Whether the security number or buyer data lands in a log or trace depends on the provider rendering {@Command} and on whether OTLP is enabled. The security number has no mapped column in the ordering entity configuration (protective), but seeded identity users carry one.
threats.objective: Confidentiality of card verification data and buyer data in logs, traces and identity storage.
prerequisites: Log or trace sink exports the structured command or message body
A reader of those sinks is an attacker or an over-broad support role
actor_assumptions: Log or telemetry reader; attacker with sink access
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: commands with card fields are logged by several behaviors and bodies are logged by string (E30, E34). Against: C-card-masking masks the number and no column maps the security number (E28); how {@Command} renders is unobserved, and the migrations snapshot is unread (G-s01-card-schema). Stage 03: IdentifiedCommandHandler also logs the inner command with {@Command} before and after it runs (E44), another site of the same pattern; it adds a log site, not independent evidence about which sinks exist or who reads them. Confidence stays low.

threats.scenario: ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED is set on every project and AllowedHosts is * on several. If the environment-variable path clears the known-proxy list, a caller who reaches a service can supply X-Forwarded-For, -Proto and -Host. Generated absolute URLs, redirect targets or client-address based logic would then follow the caller's values.
threats.objective: Integrity of URLs, redirects and client attribution derived from request headers.
prerequisites: Forwarded headers are accepted from untrusted senders (framework behaviour not observed here)
Some code uses the derived host or address (not observed)
actor_assumptions: Unauthenticated internet client
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: the setting and wildcard hosts are observed (E22, E23). Against: no code using the derived values was found, WebApp production adds HSTS (C-webapp-hsts), health endpoints are Development-only (C-health-dev-only), and the ingress in front may overwrite these headers (G12).

threats.scenario: Workflows use tag-pinned actions (checkout v4, setup-dotnet v3|v4, setup-node v4, upload-artifact v4) and pr-validation.yml has no permissions block. A compromised upstream tag would run in PR and push builds with the repository default token. The AppHost also pulls pgvector with the latest tag.
threats.objective: Integrity of the build and of the images deployed.
prerequisites: Upstream action or image tag is replaced by an attacker
Repository default token has write permissions (unobserved)
actor_assumptions: Supply-chain attacker upstream
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: tag pinning and a missing permissions block (E25), a latest tag (E1). Against: no pull_request_target (tm02:C-ci-no-pr-target), no secrets reference found by grep, and the repository default token setting is unknown.

threats.scenario: Four databases live on one Postgres server, and Aspire injects database credentials into catalog, identity, ordering, webhooks and order-processor. If those share a server login, taking over any service that holds it, including unauthenticated Catalog.API, reaches identitydb (password hashes, seeded card data) and orderingdb (addresses, payment method rows). OrderProcessor already reads orderingdb directly.
threats.objective: Confidentiality and integrity of every database on the shared server.
prerequisites: Services use the same server-level login (not observed)
Attacker executes code in or can pivot from one service
actor_assumptions: Attacker with a foothold in a service, assumed prerequisite
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: one server, one injected reference (E1), weak sample password in a development file (E16). Against: per-database roles may exist and are not shown (G3); README says the data services are evaluation containers (E26).

threats.scenario: The README says an operator deploys with local Azure credentials and that aspire destroy removes the whole resource group. Compromise or misuse of those credentials changes routes, identities and data-service credentials for every workload without touching business authorization.
threats.objective: Integrity and availability of the deployed environment.
prerequisites: Attacker holds the operator's Azure credentials or the AppHost configuration pipeline
actor_assumptions: Operator credential holder or an attacker with their session
threats.confidence_rationale: Rests on a README claim (E26) and AppHost declarations; no RBAC, deploy identity or review step was supplied, and the control-plane boundary has no owner architecture (G-s01-control-owner).

threats.scenario: PaymentProcessor turns OrderStatusChangedToStockConfirmed into OrderPaymentSucceeded from a configuration flag that is true in appsettings, with no gateway. Every order that reaches StockConfirmed is marked Paid. A copy of this template used beyond evaluation inherits a payment step that cannot fail for the customer.
threats.objective: Authenticity of the payment outcome.
prerequisites: The system is used for real orders without replacing the processor
actor_assumptions: Any customer
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: E20 and E23 show a flag-driven result. Against: README describes the deployment as evaluation and demonstration (E26), so this is the stated purpose of the sample rather than a flaw in it.

threats.scenario: Cancel and ship go through an IdentifiedCommand keyed by a caller-chosen x-requestid. When the inner command fails (cancel on a Paid or Shipped order throws, ship on a non-Paid order throws, or the order is not found), the handler swallows the failure, the transaction commits with the request id stored, and the route returns 500. A retry with the same x-requestid finds the stored id and the canned duplicate result true, so the route returns 200 OK for a cancel or ship that never happened.
threats.objective: Correct outcome reporting for cancel and ship across a retry.
prerequisites: The first attempt fails inside the inner command (a domain rule violation or a missing order)
The client retries with the same x-requestid
actor_assumptions: Client retrying after a 500; no attacker needed
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: E44 shows the request id is saved and the inner exception is swallowed so the transaction commits, and E45 shows a 500 on false for cancel and ship plus a canned true for a duplicate id. Against: the server-side flow is read from code, not run; a database-level failure that aborts the transaction could release the id (G8); whether a client reuses the same id on retry is unread (UN-005). Distinct from tm02:T-orders-request-id-consumed-failure-reported-ok because the operation, the first-attempt response (500 here, 200 there) and the state transitions differ.

threats.scenario: A forged OrderStatusChangedToPaid or OrderStatusChangedToShipped event with a chosen OrderId, product units or buyer name is serialized by Webhooks.API and POSTed to every subscription of that type, with the subscription token in a header. Subscribers receive fabricated order notifications. Split from tm02:T-bus-forged-paid-stock-and-notifications because the recipient, the affected data and the required state (an existing subscription) differ from the stock effect.
threats.objective: Authenticity of outbound webhook notifications.
prerequisites: Attacker publishes to the shared exchange
At least one subscription of that event type exists
actor_assumptions: Low-privilege workload or any holder of the broker credential
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: handlers pass the received event JSON to every subscription of the type with no owner filter (E29) and events carry no sender identity (E19). Against: broker access is an assumed prerequisite (UB2, G3), subscriptions need a reachable registration route (G1), and the payload is event JSON rather than attacker-chosen bytes.

threats.scenario: Cancel is allowed from AwaitingValidation and StockConfirmed. If a cancel lands while the payment step is in flight, PaymentProcessor still publishes a payment outcome (it does not check order state) and SetPaid becomes a silent no-op on the Cancelled order, so the order stays Cancelled with a payment outcome of success and no refund, void or compensating event exists in the code read. In the code as shipped no money moves because payment is simulated; the gap matters for a copy that adds a real gateway.
threats.objective: Consistency between a cancelled order and its payment outcome.
prerequisites: A cancel arrives while the order is in AwaitingValidation or StockConfirmed
A payment outcome event is already published or in flight
A real payment gateway replaces the simulated one for money to be affected
actor_assumptions: Customer cancelling at the wrong moment, or any authenticated caller (tm02:T-orders-cancel-ship-any-order)
threats.confidence_rationale: Supports: cancel from StockConfirmed is allowed and SetPaid acts only from StockConfirmed (E31, E32); the payment handler publishes from a configuration flag without an order check (E20); no compensation handler was found (E50). Against: payment is simulated so the shipped effect is nil (E20), the timing window is the 10 second delay plus message latency, and an order-processor or Payment reconciler outside the files read could exist (G-s02-consumer-semantics, GAP-transactions).

controls.description: Order create runs through an IdentifiedCommand keyed by x-requestid; a repeated id returns a canned success.

controls.description: The Order aggregate permits status changes only along the guarded paths (ship only from Paid; cancel not from Paid or Shipped).

controls.description: The create route masks the card number to its last 4 before the command; the security number has no mapped database column in the entity configuration read.
controls.limitations: The security number still travels through the request, command, domain event and logging behaviors; the migration snapshot and log sinks were not read. Not tested.

controls.description: Integration events are published only after the database transaction commits, using a transaction id.
controls.limitations: Outbox storage and retry were not read; commit-then-publish failure window not assessed.

controls.limitations: The webapp registration does not require PKCE; the app also ships a secret constant. Not tested.

controls.limitations: Deployed environment not observed; Identity.API and gateway headers unread (G10).

decisions.rationale: Proposed rating criteria for later caller approval: reachability (declared or observed exposure), attacker privilege needed, affected data or state, evidence confidence, and blast radius across services, on a four-level qualitative scale to be defined and weighted by the caller.
